newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen higher in early trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen higher in early trading.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to head higher in early trading on Thursday, bolstered by some strength in high techs, the semiconductors in particular.

Analysts say the catalyst will be a report by the Semiconductor Industry Association forecasting semiconductor sales growth of 3.5 percent in the fourth quarter, an indication semiconductors might be pulling out of a year-long slump.
"This will be helpful to the chip-makers and it might give us a decent start," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities.
Traders will also digest the latest U.S. data on consuer spending.
Consumers spent frugally in September despite solid gains in incomes, the Commerce Department said, and socked more money into savings.

Spending rose a slim 0.1 percent, or $3.4 billion, to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $5.18 trillion after a 0.5 percent August gain. Incomes from wages, salaries and all other sources climbed 0.6 percent, or $41.5 billion, to a rate of $6.54 trillion after a 0.5 percent August rise.
